page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 446 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this server sits primarily in the lower tiers for modern compute tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25 percent. Memory read bandwidth is also weak, though large block memory write bandwidth achieves average tier results. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware flags such as AES, AVX, AVX512F, and BMI2, though decompression and compression tasks score poorly to weakly.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and integrated 446 GB local SSD, this server offers a self-contained resource profile for workloads requiring persistent local storage without relying on network-attached disks. However, its older Broadwell-generation processor limits its efficiency for high-throughput database operations or modern LLM inference, where it scores in the bottom 10 percent to 25 percent. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, legacy application hosting, basic web serving, and lightweight development environments that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and local SSD storage but do not demand high-performance compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, 446 GB of local SSD storage, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates modest performance, with single-core and multi-core CPU metrics, memory read bandwidth, and database operations generally ranking in the bottom 25 percent of tested servers. Large block memory write bandwidth and small-model LLM inference perform at average levels. Lacking modern instruction sets like AMX or AVX-VNNI, this instance is best suited for legacy general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and lightweight development tasks that require dedicated CPU resources and local SSD storage rather than high-performance compute.
